adds.title: Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre and Others, Case No. 2024/070075 - High Court of South Africa, Gauteng Local Division, Johannesburg (Fisher J), judgment of 10 November 2025
adds.summary: National placement standard governing trans prisoners in every province including Eastern Cape: the judgment records that DCS agrees that, under the regulations to the Correctional Services Act relating to accommodation of vulnerable inmates and the DCS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), inmates should be accommodated in cells appropriate to their gender identity where feasible and safe; DCS further conceded its own SOPs prescribe single-cell accommodation for transgender inmates. The Equality Court, applying these instruments, ordered the DCS to accommodate the complainant in a single cell or in the same cell with inmates of the same gender identity. This is the operative rule for where trans prisoners are housed in Eastern Cape correctional centres (e.g., St Albans, Mthatha, East London), no province-specific trans-placement case being on record.

records.note: No Eastern Cape-specific trans-prisoner housing case, DCS decision, or media report was located (1 Wikipedia full-text search; project fetch cache reuse). Eastern Cape correctional centres have no documented trans-specific placement data or special unit; the governing rule is the national DCS SOP framework below - cells appropriate to the inmate's gender identity where feasible and safe - as recorded in the November 2025 Gauteng High Court (Equality Court) judgment in the Mokoena case. The record's existing sources contain no EC prison-housing datum either.

adds.title: Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre and Others, Case No. 2024/070075 - High Court of South Africa, Gauteng Local Division, Johannesburg (Fisher J), judgment of 10 November 2025
adds.summary: The only documented determination of where trans prisoners are housed in Gauteng. Mokoena, a transgender woman serving life, is held at Johannesburg Correctional Centre: initially housed in Medium A section where she could express her gender identity (long hair, makeup, women's clothing); later transferred to Medium C section; at the time of the judgment she was housed in C Single Section, a segregated/solitary-confinement unit of Medium C, and - despite requesting a single cell - was accommodated with cisgender male cellmates (first two cisgender gay men, then one cisgender male), which DCS justified by overcrowding. The court found the DCS's SOPs prescribe accommodation appropriate to gender identity where feasible and safe and that no basis existed for refusing single accommodation, ordering DCS to house her in a single cell or with inmates of the same gender identity and to enforce its transgender-inmate SOPs.

adds.title: Media Statement: National Preventive Mechanism welcomes the High Court ruling affirming the rights of transgender persons in correctional facilities
adds.summary: SAHRC (as South Africa's OPCAT National Preventive Mechanism) welcomes the 10 November 2025 judgment of the Gauteng Division of the High Court, Johannesburg, in Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (Case No. 2024/070075), which found the DCS engaged in unfair discrimination and harassment of transgender inmate Nthabiseng Mokoena - including by failing to provide appropriate accommodation - and ordered the DCS to enforce its SOPs on transgender inmates and house her in a single cell or with inmates of the same gender identity. Confirms the Correctional Services Act vulnerable-inmate accommodation framework as the operative housing standard in Gauteng's correctional centres.

records.note: Gauteng's trans-prisoner housing answer rests on the Mokoena judgment (10 Nov 2025, Equality Court, Fisher J): trans prisoners are housed in male-side sections of correctional centres (Johannesburg Correctional Centre: Medium A, then Medium C, then the C Single Section segregation unit), shared with cisgender male cellmates where single cells are refused, with the court ordering single-cell or same-gender-identity co-housing per the DCS's own SOPs. One Wikipedia full-text search returned no additional Gauteng-specific source; both adds reuse the project's cached, verified fetches (http 200, re-confirmed).
